synthesis.trait: Doug quietly handles hosting/service duties during family gatherings (serving food and drinks)
Doug offers John gentle companionship and consideration for his emotional state without pressuring him
Doug feels professional inferiority to John and seeks his validation/approval as a fellow cop
Doug acts to protectively control situations/people to prevent conflict
Doug uses his police access and initiative to assist John's investigation
Doug defends Mackie's competence and reputation as a cop
Doug maintains a calm, composed demeanor even when personally challenged or insulted

turning_points.trait_it_relates_to: Doug uses his police access and initiative to assist John's investigation
turning_points.what_changes: Doug moves from passively handing John a folder of Mackie's case files to proactively tracing phone tower pings on his own initiative, digging into the evidence trail unasked and reporting a concrete lead location.

turning_points.trait_it_relates_to: Doug acts to protectively control situations/people to prevent conflict
turning_points.what_changes: Doug's protective effort escalates to repeated verbal pleading and warnings about jurisdiction, but unlike his simple, successful restraint of Trudy earlier, this attempt fails outright when John hangs up on him, exposing a limit to his protective authority.

turning_points.trait_it_relates_to: Doug uses his police access and initiative to assist John's investigation
turning_points.what_changes: Doug now facilitates an unofficial, off-the-books interrogation of a suspect in a secluded non-official room, a markedly riskier and more procedurally compromising act of assistance than tracing phone records through legitimate channels.

turning_points.trait_it_relates_to: Doug defends Mackie's competence and reputation as a cop
turning_points.what_changes: Doug moves from a mild factual denial ("never heard of it") to personally absorbing John's criticism of the report as an insult against himself and Mackie, deflecting emotionally rather than simply correcting the record.

turning_points.trait_it_relates_to: Doug offers John gentle companionship and consideration for his emotional state without pressuring him
turning_points.what_changes: Doug moves from silent companionship and offering a cigarette to directly confronting John with a painful personal truth about his history with Cheyenne, risking John's anger to say something necessary.

turning_points.trait_it_relates_to: Doug offers John gentle companionship and consideration for his emotional state without pressuring him
turning_points.what_changes: Doug continues the same confrontation without a gap, going further to name that Holly could have been John's own daughter, deepening the painful truth-telling just begun.

turning_points.trait_it_relates_to: Doug maintains a calm, composed demeanor even when personally challenged or insulted
turning_points.what_changes: Doug maintains composure against direct, deeply personal hostility ("Fuck you") from someone he cares about, a far higher emotional cost than absorbing professional criticism of a case report.

turning_points.trait_it_relates_to: Doug feels professional inferiority to John and seeks his validation/approval as a fellow cop
turning_points.what_changes: Whereas Doug once envied John's LA-cop status and sought his approval, he now explicitly says "I feel sorry for you, John," reversing the earlier admiration/deference dynamic into pity.

turning_points.trait_it_relates_to: Doug offers John gentle companionship and consideration for his emotional state without pressuring him
turning_points.what_changes: Doug moves from casual porch companionship to being the bearer of devastating news of a child's death, delivered with explicit empathy ("I'm sorry, John. We really tried."), a far higher-stakes instance of the same gentle attentiveness.

turning_points.trait_it_relates_to: Doug offers John gentle companionship and consideration for his emotional state without pressuring him
turning_points.what_changes: Immediately after delivering the news, Doug offers to take on the burden of telling Cheyenne himself, continuing the same protective gentleness before yielding to John's insistence.

turning_points.trait_it_relates_to: Doug acts to protectively control situations/people to prevent conflict
turning_points.what_changes: Doug physically stays back and gives John space to approach Cheyenne alone, enacting the deference to John's wishes just established in the prior beat.

turning_points.trait_it_relates_to: Doug maintains a calm, composed demeanor even when personally challenged or insulted
turning_points.what_changes: For the first time Doug's composure visibly cracks (shaky voice, stammering) -- but only when the subject turns specifically to Trudy, revealing a personal vulnerability that even sustained professional and personal insults never exposed.

turning_points.trait_it_relates_to: Doug maintains a calm, composed demeanor even when personally challenged or insulted
turning_points.what_changes: Doug's anxiety about Trudy continues and intensifies immediately after, now visibly upset and pacing, needing John to calm him rather than the reverse.

turning_points.trait_it_relates_to: Doug maintains a calm, composed demeanor even when personally challenged or insulted
turning_points.what_changes: Doug remains rattled and anxious, still seeking connection by approaching with coffee, even as John brushes past and dismisses his concern, continuing the unresolved vulnerability.
